text_snippet: La universidad en el territorio: una experiencia de inmersión social en arquitectura en la Universidad Iberoamericana Ciudad de México The University in the Territory: An Experience of Social Immersion in Architecture at Universidad Iberoamericana Ciudad de México A universidade no território: uma experiência de imersão social em arquitetura na Universidad Iberoamericana Ciudad de México This article reports on a pedagogical experience carried out as part of the University Social Action and Formation Pathway (FASU) at Universidad Iberoamericana Mexico City, within the Projects III course of the Architecture program. The project integrates participatory action research (PAR) with the principles of Ignatian pedagogy to foster situated, critical, and transformative learning. In collaboration with the organization CIAS por la Paz and La Malinche community, students engaged in participatory diagnostics, social mapping, and collaborative workshops aimed at rebuilding the social fabric and defending the territory. The process enabled an understanding of architecture as an ethical and political practice oriented toward the common good. The results reveal a threefold impact—educational, community, and institutional—by strengthening technical and social competencies, fostering connections with Jesuit social works, and advancing the university’s mission of justice and peace. Together with three researchers from the University of Ibagué, they co-created strategies for training, management, and community engagement. Tools such as social mapping, timelines, project formulation workshops, field journals, and self-care exercises were used. title: Estudio de casos y evaluación formativa: una práctica de enseñanza situada en Cali, Colombia Case-Based Learning and Formative Feedback: A Situated Teaching Practice in Cali, Colombia Estudo de caso e retroalimentação formativa: uma prática de ensino situada em Cali, Colômbia
text_snippet: Estudio de casos y evaluación formativa: una práctica de enseñanza situada en Cali, Colombia Case-Based Learning and Formative Feedback: A Situated Teaching Practice in Cali, Colombia Estudo de caso e retroalimentação formativa: uma prática de ensino situada em Cali, Colômbia This article systematizes a pedagogical experience developed in the course Developmental Psychology II at a private university in Cali, Colombia, aimed at promoting more reflective, analytical, and contextualized learning through formative assessment, case-based learning, and formative assessment. Implemented over three consecutive semesters, the redesign addressed two needs: strengthening the connection between theory and real-world contexts and transforming assessment into a practice oriented toward learning. Using a qualitative systematization-of-experiences approach, the study analyzed pedagogical documents and the perceptions of 36 students who voluntarily completed an anonymous open-ended questionnaire. Findings indicate that, from the students’ perspective, case-based work supported a more situated understanding of concepts, as well as argumentation, critical analysis, and greater sensitivity to social and human realities. The problem addressed does not lie in the absence of connections between the NEM and university-based social responsibility practices, but rather in the conceptual ambiguity through which such articulations are framed, making it difficult to delineate their scope and tensions within higher education. title: Descolonizando la educación: la educación propia como herramienta de sentido a partir de una cartografía de experiencias Decolonizing Education: Self-Determined Education as a Tool of Meaning based on a Cartography of Experiences Descolonizando a educação: a própria educação como ferramenta de significado a partir de uma cartografia de experiências
text_snippet: Descolonizando la educación: la educación propia como herramienta de sentido a partir de una cartografía de experiencias Decolonizing Education: Self-Determined Education as a Tool of Meaning based on a Cartography of Experiences Descolonizando a educação: a própria educação como ferramenta de significado a partir de uma cartografia de experiências This article develops a critical reflection on the processes of educational decolonization in Latin American contexts, situating self-determined education as a central axis for the construction of meaning, identity and cultural resistance in the face of hegemonic educational systems that have reproduced colonial matrices of knowledge, power and being. From a theoretical-critical position, and through an approach to a cartography of self-determined educational experiences, the way in which these dominant logics have configured exclusionary educational ontologies, limiting the recognition of ancestral, community and territorial knowledge in contemporary schools, is problematized. The text’s thesis is that educational decolonization is only possible through the full recognition of epistemic plurality and the restitution of the pedagogical sovereignty of peoples. title: Microhistoria y memoria viva: objetos, voces y aula como laboratorio para enseñar historia escolar crítica Microhistory and Living Memory: Objects, Voices, and the Classroom as a Laboratory for Teaching Critical School History
text_snippet: Microhistoria y memoria viva: objetos, voces y aula como laboratorio para enseñar historia escolar crítica Microhistory and Living Memory: Objects, Voices, and the Classroom as a Laboratory for Teaching Critical School History This article analyzes history teaching through the reconstruction of family memories and everyday objects, validated as legitimate sources of historical knowledge. The central purpose is to understand how a pedagogical strategy based on participatory action research (PAR) promotes the formation of critical historical subjects at the Colegio Nacionalizado La Presentación, in Duitama (Boyacá, Colombia), where a “Center of Interest” of the Ministry of National Education is implemented. The methodology engaged tenth-grade students as co-investigators, using narrative and ethnographic techniques to recover meanings from the past on a micro-historical scale. In this process, reading Carlo Ginzburg’s The Cheese and the Worms acted as a pedagogical device to challenge hegemonic narratives and strengthen participatory praxis in the classroom. Under a principle of horizontality, participants collectively designed the inquiry instruments, prioritizing the ethics of intergenerational dialogue and situated motivation. From a qualitative and situated perspective, these practices are understood not as isolated actions, but as forms of pedagogical knowledge production that emerge from territory, experience, and the social conditions that shape public education. The article argues that such practices hold valuable insights for the initial training of future teachers in higher education, particularly during the early semesters of teacher education programs. Drawing on the theoretical advances of the research, the paper reflects on the existing gap between universities and schools and highlights the need for a university-community dialogue that recognizes teachers as knowledge producers rather than mere implementers of policies. text_snippet: Asistentes de inteligencia artificial en la generación de ideas iniciales para ensayos académicos The Role of Artificial Intelligence Assistants in Generating Initial Ideas for Academic Essays in Higher Education O papel dos assistentes de inteligência artificial na geração de ideias iniciais para ensaios académicos no ensino superior This study analyzes the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the initial phase of academic essay writing, specifically in idea generation. The objective was to identify strategies, tasks, and perceptions related to the use of AI in the Literacy Leveling Courses at the National University of Colombia, Bogotá campus. Eighty-two students participated through self-administered questionnaires, and ten through semi-structured interviews. A mixed-methods design was used, combining qualitative analysis (inductive-deductive coding in ATLAS.ti) and descriptive quantitative analysis. The results show that AI is used for brainstorming, topic delimitation, argument organization, and overcoming initial writer’s block. Reported benefits include clarity, efficiency, and cognitive support, while limitations involve inaccuracy, lack of depth, and artificial style. This scenario requires trained professionals who are, at the same time, reflective citizens of their reality and who think critically. title: La educación en museos como acto transformador: raíces comunitarias para territorios de paz Museum Education as a Transformative Act: Community Roots for Territories of Peace Educação em museus como ato transformador: raízes comunitárias para territórios de paz
text_snippet: La educación en museos como acto transformador: raíces comunitarias para territorios de paz Museum Education as a Transformative Act: Community Roots for Territories of Peace Educação em museus como ato transformador: raízes comunitárias para territórios de paz This paper explores how education in community museums becomes a key tool for transformative education in contexts marked by armed conflict. It examines two significant Colombian experiences: the Itinerant Museum of Memory and Identity of the Montes de María (MIM), and the Community Museum of Guainía, both located in territories that have suffered the consequences of armed conflict. The essay demonstrates how education, understood as a situated and participatory practice, enables the reconstruction of the social fabric, the affirmation of collective identities, and the projection of possible futures rooted in local knowledge. In these museums, the community plays a central role in the educational process—not merely as recipients, but as active creators of narratives, symbols, and methodologies. The essay is grounded in a theoretical framework that connects museum education, the role of community museums, and their contributions to peacebuilding. title: Cuando los profesores aprenden a jugar When Teachers Learn to Play Quando os professores aprendem a jogar
text_snippet: Cuando los profesores aprenden a jugar When Teachers Learn to Play Quando os professores aprendem a jogar This research analyzes, through the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology, the acceptance of a gamified tool called FINATIC by secondary school teachers. It identifies the factors influencing their decision to use the tool in the classroom. A mixed-methods design was applied, combining PLS-SEM analysis and text mining on interviews with 25 teachers from secondary schools in Colombia. The results show that prior knowledge of gamified tools and the teacher’s subjective perception are the most influential factors in their acceptance. Although FINATIC is perceived as innovative and useful, its effective implementation is limited by technological and customization barriers. Gamification is seen as a powerful strategy for youth financial education, but its adoption requires adequate institutional conditions and teacher training. This study contributes an analytical model of teacher acceptance (MADEM-HG) and responds to the question: What happens when teachers play? It turns out they are willing to innovate—provided they have the right context and support.

The main objective was to explore the motivations derived from family, school, and community contexts that affect students’ decisions related to more constructive life choices, particularly access to and retention in higher education focused on English learning. The study followed a descriptive design with a mixed-methods approach, using simple random sampling and involving 23 students (12 males and 11 females) aged between 16 and 17. Data were collected through surveys, semi-structured interviews, and direct observation. The results revealed that the most influential motivational factors were: (1) the success of family members in English-related careers, (2) the emphasis and quality of English instruction at school, (3) community support and accessibility of higher education, and (4) positive perceptions of English in the media and social dynamics. title: La calidad de interacciones profesor estudiante y el desempeño en cuarto de primaria The Quality of Teacher-Student Interactions and Performance in Fourth Grade A qualidade das interações professor-aluno e o desempenho na quarta série
text_snippet: La calidad de interacciones profesor estudiante y el desempeño en cuarto de primaria The Quality of Teacher-Student Interactions and Performance in Fourth Grade A qualidade das interações professor-aluno e o desempenho na quarta série This article analyzes the association between the quality of teacher-student interactions and the academic and socioemotional development of fourth-grade students in two public charter schools in Bogotá (Colombia). Using a correlational design, linear regression models were applied to estimate the relationship between the dimensions of closeness and conflict—measured through the STRS—and student performance in Spanish, Mathematics, and socioemotional skills. The results show that relationships characterized by greater closeness are positively associated with performance in Spanish and socioemotional development, while conflict is negatively associated with performance in Mathematics and with five out of the six socioemotional skills evaluated. These findings remain significant even after controlling for family, individual, and teacher-related variables, and are consistent with previous research. The study thus highlights the importance of strengthening teachers’ capacities to foster high-quality interactions as a key component of child development in school settings.

title: Maestros-en-formación: hacerse consentido en la enseñanza Teachers-in-Training: The Meaningful Becoming of the Teacher through Teaching Professores-em-formação: dar sentido ao ensino
text_snippet: Maestros-en-formación: hacerse consentido en la enseñanza Teachers-in-Training: The Meaningful Becoming of the Teacher through Teaching Professores-em-formação: dar sentido ao ensino What makes studying at a normal school distinctive in the preparation of future teachers is that training occurs through the practice of teaching. This is a relational experience that extends beyond the curriculum and transcends the classroom, particularly because individuals inhabit both the positions of student and teacher. This article explores this dynamic through a school-based ethnography conducted in three normal schools located in predominantly rural areas. It argues that being addressed as a “teacher” constitutes an ethical event—an interpellation that prompts the subject to recognize themselves as in formation: a moment of recognition and reception that activates knowledge in action. Teaching thus constitutes a doing-knowing in which an inventive capacity emerges that exceeds the boundaries of institutional structures, even as it is made possible by them. From this perspective, the article reaffirms the centrality of teaching as a formative experience and offers insights for re-signifying their place and contribution within the national teacher education system.

title: El arte como estrategia para promover un pensamiento científico visible en educación infantil Art as a Strategy to Promote Visible Scientific Thinking in Early Childhood Education A arte como estratégia para promover o pensamento científico visível na educacão infantil
text_snippet: El arte como estrategia para promover un pensamiento científico visible en educación infantil Art as a Strategy to Promote Visible Scientific Thinking in Early Childhood Education A arte como estratégia para promover o pensamento científico visível na educacão infantil The development of scientific thinking skills in early childhood through art has been scarcely explored within pedagogical practices. This article presents an innovative learning experience for kindergarten children from an official educational institution in Cimitarra (Santander, Colombia). The three projects that comprise this experience (My Body is Wonderful, My Family is Special, and Guardians of Nature) combine artistic languages and scientific thinking to play a fundamental role in the integral formation of the being. A qualitative approach through the methodological design of the participatory action research (PAR) was adopted, using observation schemes and notes records as instruments. A pedagogical reflection of the children’s experiences in the three proposed projects, which involved visible thinking, art, and science, concluded that these strategies promoted significant learning and contributed to the continuous improvement of the students’ scientific and artistic thinking through the guiding activities.

title: Lived experiences of metacognitive awareness emerging among teachersin training Experiencias vividas de la conciencia metacognitiva que emerge entre docentes en formación Experiências vividas de consciência metacognitiva emergentes entre professores em formação
text_snippet: Lived experiences of metacognitive awareness emerging among teachersin training Experiencias vividas de la conciencia metacognitiva que emerge entre docentes en formación Experiências vividas de consciência metacognitiva emergentes entre professores em formação This study examines the transformative experiences of pre-service teachers as they develop metacognitive awareness during their pedagogical practices. Grounded in Husserlian transcendental phenomenology and analyzed using Colaizzi’s method, the research explores how these future educators become aware of their own cognitive and reflective processes in authentic classroom settings. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and reflective journals from 12 participants at a Colombian university. The analysis reveals a progression characterized by an initial disruption in routine teaching practices, followed by the emergence of metacognitive awareness, sustained reflection, and the subsequent adaptive management of classroom challenges. These findings indicate that specific moments of self-reflection contribute to the development of a resilient and reflective teaching identity, which, in turn, supports the continuous refinement of pedagogical strategies. text_snippet: Explorando seres vivos en la ciénaga San Rafael de Cortina, Colombia: proyecto para fortalecer el pensamiento científico infantil y la conciencia ambiental Exploring Living Beings in San Rafael de Cortina Swamp in Colombia: A Project to Strengthen Children’s Scientific Thinking and Environmental Awareness Explorando os seres vivos no pântano de San Rafael de Cortina, Colômbia: um projeto para fortalecer o pensamento científico e a consciência ambiental das crianas This article presents a pedagogical experience that seeks to promote scientific thinking and environmental awareness in preschool boys and girls through the observation, inquiry and exploration of a swamp, recognized as a natural ecosystem rich in plant and animal species. The project was framed within the strategy of the Ondas Program of the Ministry of Science and Technology. It aimed to identify, via an inquiry-based methodology, native plant and animal species that surround the San Rafael de Cortina swamp in Magangué, Bolívar (Colombia). The systematization process used a qualitative methodology, which included the observation and description of the children’s attitudes and skills, their experience, and their learning. This study uses a critical and participatory research model to analyze how Computational Thinking (CT) skills are used and developed in students from Arts and Humanities programs and proposes an introductory CT course specifically designed for this context. The course addressed CT concepts and was structured around a transition from activities such as coding, decoding, and creating poems with algorithms, through text marking with HTML, to introductory programming using Processing in p5.js. text_snippet: Sensibilidad intercultural, migración y enseñanza de las ciencias: la concepción de Patricia, profesora de ciencias naturales Intercultural Sensitivity, Migration, and Science Teaching: Patricia’s Perspective, a Natural Sciences Teacher Sensibilidade intercultural, migraão e ensino de ciências: a concepão de Patricia, professora de ciências naturais This article is situated in the field of science teaching with an intercultural approach. It reports on a broader study aimed at identifying and interpreting science teachers’ conceptions of intercultural sensitivity in relation to migration. To achieve this, the study examines the reflections of Patricia, a 45-year-old science teacher from Bogotá (Colombia). A qualitative, interpretative approach was employed, which involved the design, application, and analysis of semi-structured interviews. Eliciting situations were incorporated to construct the interviewee’s narrative, analyzed with NVivo software. The findings reveal that the teacher acknowledges various types of knowledge in the classroom but primarily validates scientific knowledge, structuring her pedagogical practices accordingly. Additionally, her intercultural sensitivity reflects an ethnocentric stance rooted in institutional frameworks and curriculum defense. The research focused on identifying the themes and discursive strategies that shape this project, with emphasis on its didactic and formative nature. The main hypothesis is that the company uses narratives rooted in moral panic to reinforce conservative values. A qualitative design was adopted, using the documentary series “Pátria Educadora”—comprising three episodes available on the company’s YouTube channel—as the primary unit of analysis. The sample was intentional, based on the thematic relevance of the material to the discourse on education. Data were analyzed using Atlas.ti 7 software, with Theodor W. This article presents an experience focused on learning about the life cycle and ecological role of earthworms in preschool students through playful scientific strategies. The project takes place in a classroom of 5- and 6-year-old children and addresses the need to implement a practical and experiential approach to stimulate scientific skills from early childhood. An experiential and constructivist approach was adopted, thus children actively participated in observing earthworms, using magnifying glasses, and creating terrariums, fostering respectful interactions with living beings. The results showed a strengthening of scientific curiosity and the acquisition of basic knowledge about the earthworm life cycle. Teamwork and shared responsibility for the collective terrarium promoted empathy, collaboration, and respect for nature. text_snippet: Representaciones sobre las prácticas curriculares en colegios colombianos y brasileros Representations of Internships in Colombian and Brazilian Schools Representações sobre os estágios em colégios colombianos y brasileiros This article presents the results of a postdoctoral research study aimed at identifying and analyzing the perceptions of school administrators, public school teachers, and interns regarding initial practical training through case studies, two conducted in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and four in Bogotá, Colombia. Using a qualitative approach, the verbal statements of 28 participants, men and women, were analyzed through interviews and focus groups. The findings indicate that practical training appears to depend on the guidelines established by school management, the active role of those involved, and the formative background of teachers. In conclusion, decisions regarding time management, as well as the active and continuous participation of all stakeholders, are key factors in the consolidation of internships.

title: Cambio climático, educación en emergencias y currículo: aportes para la formación de profesores en Colombia Climate Change, Education in Emergencies and Curriculum: Contributions to the Training of Teachers in Colombia Mudanças climáticas, educação em emergências e currículo: contribuições para a formação de professores na Colômbia
text_snippet: Cambio climático, educación en emergencias y currículo: aportes para la formación de profesores en Colombia Climate Change, Education in Emergencies and Curriculum: Contributions to the Training of Teachers in Colombia Mudanças climáticas, educação em emergências e currículo: contribuições para a formação de professores na Colômbia The effects of climate change affect the right to education in different ways. During emergency situations due to socio-natural phenomena, education is usually denied or postponed. The training of teachers, both in the initial stage and in practice, on topics such as climate change, natural disasters, and humanitarian crises offers an opportunity for these actors who energize the educational system to confront the environmental crises that are occurring and those that are coming. This essay provides some data on the climate impact on education, the development of education in emergencies in Colombia, the need to adapt the curriculum when facing humanitarian crisis, and the importance of teacher training in these fields.

text_snippet: Salud mental en la infancia: ¿qué nos dicen los niños y niñas en la escuela? Mental Health in Childhood: What Do Children Say About It at School? Saúde mental na infância: o que as crianças nos contam na escola? Mental health has been the subject of multiple investigations in different fields of knowledge. While there are definitions framed in laws and models, there is no consensus. In recent years, research on mental health has noted the increasing number of disorders and needs among children. However, it was only recently that studies began to focus on what constitutes mental health in childhood. However, in this discourse on mental health in childhood, children have often been rendered invisible by an adult-centric narrative that attempts to make the best decisions for them. In this context, the research that frames this article aimed to contribute to the conceptualization of children’s mental health in the school setting, taking as its main element the meanings that children have constructed about it. Using a qualitative methodology with a narrative design, the meaning of mental health in childhood was examined in children, teachers, and parents. As a result, a theoretical approach to the research phenomenon was constructed, which primarily reflected children’s voices. However, at the official educational institution in Santander (Colombia) where this experience took place, located in a vulnerable social context, persistent difficulties in mathematics were identified, reflected in low results on external tests, student demotivation, and negative attitudes toward the subject. text_snippet: Interseccionalidad y justicia epistémica en el currículo de educación superior en Argentina, Brasil y Colombia Intersectionality and Epistemic Justice in the Higher Education Curriculum in Argentina, Brazil, and Colombia Interseccionalidade e justiça epistêmica no currículo do ensino superior na Argentina, Brasil e Colômbia This article explores and analyzes the intersections between gender, “race”, class, and territory in the curricula of three teacher training programs at three public higher education institutions (HEIs) in Argentina, Brazil, and Colombia. To do so, it examines how these intersections are addressed in the curricula and the implications this has for teacher training. It also seeks to make visible counter-hegemonic curricular practices that are being implemented and that propose reinterpretations that challenge Eurocentrism and epistemic injustice within the curricula. This research, framed within the sociology of education and ethno-racial studies, from an intersectional perspective, was developed with a qualitative and sociocritical approach. title: Interculturalidad y formación docente en Colombia: el aporte de las licenciaturas en etnoeducación (1994-2024) Interculturality and teacher training in Colombia: the contribution of bachelor's degrees in Ethnoeducation (1994-2024) Interculturalidade e formação de professores na Colômbia: a contribuição dos cursos de bacharelado em Etnoeducação (1994-2024)
text_snippet: Interculturalidad y formación docente en Colombia: el aporte de las licenciaturas en etnoeducación (1994-2024) Interculturality and teacher training in Colombia: the contribution of bachelor's degrees in Ethnoeducation (1994-2024) Interculturalidade e formação de professores na Colômbia: a contribuição dos cursos de bacharelado em Etnoeducação (1994-2024) Since 1994, university programs offering degrees in ethno-education have emerged in different regions of Colombia. The approach underlying these teacher training processes draws on the perspective of ethno-education formalized in Law 115 of 1994 and Decree 804 of 1994. The approach on which these teacher training processes are based reflects the perspective of ethno-education formalized in Law 115 of 1994 and Decree 804 of 1995, regulations that recognize the education of ethnic groups and the right of indigenous peoples and Afro-descendant communities to cultural control over their education. The embryo of an intercultural teacher training system in the field of Colombian higher education is associated with this phenomenon, which I call university ethno-education. This article revisits historical and political elements from three decades of its journey, with the aim of highlighting its progress and contributions to Colombian teacher training, an area in which these experiences are not yet recognized.

text_snippet: Un camino pedagógico desde las artes para la armonización y revitalización de los lugares y círculos del agua A Pedagogical Path from the Arts for the Harmonization and Revitalization of Water Places and Circles Um caminho pedagógico a partir das artes para a harmonização e revitalização de espaços e círculos aquáticos This article seeks to raise awareness of the importance of water care through the sharing of knowledge. It delves into pedagogical processes related to the arts, especially music, around harmonization and sensitive paths for the revitalization of water circles, affected today by the growth of cities and the devastation of vital water sources, which is presented as a problem in the short and long term. It is based on research developed as a student and teacher in a context of interculturality, autochthonous education, and experiences shared with managers, environmentalists, artists, Muysca teachers, youth, children, and grandparents, who contribute with their questions and stories in scenarios where learning takes place from the territory.

From this perspective, it reflects on three issues that serve as disruptive bets on decolonization, dignity and social justice, since they respond politically and pedagogically to weave a more equitable and inclusive education and society: the first is ethno-education, understood as an ethno-political project and an educational policy; the second is university ethno-education, which translates as the emergence of bachelor’s degree programs in ethno-education; and finally, intercultural education, which is performed by ethno-educators based on the principles and foundations of ethno-education. This reflective article proposes that ethno-educators are transcending ethno-education towards intercultural education, since the former has a regulatory framework that restricts its execution in more diverse contexts. text_snippet: El encanto narrativo de La muñeca negra con niños y niñas de preescolar en Buenaventura,Colombia The Narrative Charm of The Black Doll with Kindergarten Children in Buenaventura, Colombia O encanto narrativo Da boneca negra em crianças de pré-escola em Buenaventura, Colômbia The understanding of narratives favors the development of a community’s oral tradition, and one way to achieve this is by encouraging short story reading. For this reason, this research was based on the story La muñeca negra (The Black Doll), which was used as a pedagogical strategy to strengthen the socio-cultural territorial dynamics of preschool children in an official educational institution located in Buenaventura, Colombia.
